title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
gist: Cloudflare released Traces in open beta, turning proxy-layer steps (security rules, transforms, cache, routing, Workers, origin) into OpenTelemetry spans exportable over OTLP. Alongside it, pricing for Traces and Workers Tracing moves on December 1, 2026 from per-span billing to ingested-data and retention charges.

insights.claim: Cloudflare Traces extends automatic tracing from Workers to the whole request path, so security rules, transformations, cache decisions, routing, Worker execution and origin handling appear as OpenTelemetry spans without instrumentation.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Closes the visibility gap in the proxy layer; a differentiator for Cloudflare's developer platform against observability vendors.
insights.quote: Security rules, transformations, cache decisions, routing, Worker execution, and origin handling now appear as OpenTelemetry spans

insights.claim: Before Traces, a proxied request's trace showed the client and the application with everything in between inferred from logs and configuration.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Explains the demand for proxy-level spans.

insights.claim: In Cloudflare's example, a cache-miss request spent 527ms of its 539ms on getting a response from the origin, which span-level timing makes visible.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Illustrates the diagnostic value of nested cache/upstream/origin spans.
insights.locator: The questions Cloudflare uses as examples

insights.claim: Traces accepts a W3C traceparent header and can forward a new one to the origin, so Cloudflare spans join traces started upstream; an incoming propagation policy limits accepting context from arbitrary clients.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Interoperability with existing tracing makes adoption less lock-in-prone.
insights.locator: Context propagation is what makes it more than a Cloudflare-only view

insights.claim: Sampling uses Cloudflare's rules engine: a low baseline rate (e.g. 1%) with Trace Rules overriding it for matching traffic such as one customer's hostname or a temporary debug header.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Targeted sampling lets teams control observability volume and, now, cost.
insights.locator: Sampling runs on the same rules engine

insights.claim: Spans export over OTLP to any compatible backend via an account-level destination, which Cloudflare frames as a commitment to OpenTelemetry and data portability across observability tools.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Cloudflare positions as a telemetry source rather than a closed observability silo.

insights.claim: Through the Cloudflare Observability MCP server, a coding agent can query traces via the SQL API, compare failed with successful traces and tie divergences to repository code, making telemetry something an agent reads rather than a person watches.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Observability products are being redesigned for agent consumption.

insights.claim: From December 1, 2026 Cloudflare replaces per-span billing (announced for October 1) with charges on ingested data and retention, the second pricing change in two months.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Pricing churn is a risk for teams budgeting tracing on Cloudflare.
insights.locator: Teams already using Workers Tracing should note the pricing change

insights.claim: Free plan includes 0.5GB/day ingestion with seven-day retention; Paid and Enterprise include 50GB ingestion and 10GB-month storage per cycle, then $0.25 per GB ingested and $0.10 per GB-month stored.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Gives unit prices to compare with other observability vendors.

insights.claim: Charging by volume rather than by span is the more consequential half of the change because sampling decisions now map directly to the bill.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Teams should keep baseline sampling low and escalate only for investigated traffic.
insights.quote: Sampling decisions now map directly to a bill
insights.locator: Charging by volume rather than by span

insights.claim: Coverage is partial: planned additions include DDoS rules, Access, Workflows, Queues and Pipelines instrumentation, authenticated context propagation, ad hoc single-request tracing and OpenTelemetry API support in Workers.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Beta is incomplete; full adoption depends on these roadmap items.
